la:verb:dehisco.gloss: to part, divide, split open, gape, yawn
senses: to part, divide, split open, gape, yawn
la:verb:dehisco.html:
dĕ-hisco, hīvi (in the
inf. dehisse, v.the foll.), ĕre, v. n., to part, divide, go apart; to split open; to gape, to yawn (excepting once in Varr., not ante-Aug.): dehisse terram, Müll.; so of the yawning earth,; ; : unda dehiscens,: neque enim ante dehiscent Attonitae magna ora domus,: ex intervallo os paulum dehiscit,: cymba rimis,; cf.: navigium,springs aleak,: dehiscens intervallis acies,: dehiscere ingentibus rimis, Fragm. init.: rosa paullatim rubescens dehiscit ac sese pandit,; cf. ib. § 18 fin.: thynni pinguescunt in tantum ut dehiscant,burst open,.

la:adv:dehinc.gloss: from here, from here on in, hence, henceforth, from this time on, in the future, at a later stage (in the story)
senses: from here, from here on in, hence, henceforth, from this time on, in the future, at a later stage (in the story)
immediately afterward, afterwards, after that, thereafter, thereupon, then, next
from this place on, from here on
la:adv:dehinc.html:
dĕ-hinc (in the poets freq. monosyllabic, e. g. ; ; ; cf. . Dissyllabic in ; ; ; ; ; ).—
Adv., from this place forth, from here, hence.
In space.
Lit. (not ante-Aug. and rare): interiora Cedrosii, dehinc Persae habitant,; : dehinc ab Syria usque ad, etc.,. —
Transf.
In the order of succession (poet.): ex fumo dare lucem Cogitat ut speciosa dehinc miracula promat,; .—
Like our hence, to indicate a consequence (only in the foll. places): sequi decretum'st, dehinc conjicito ceterum,; .—
In time, with or without respect to the terminus a quo (freq. in Plaut. and Ter. and since the Aug. period; not in Cic., Caes., or Quint.).
With respect to the term. a quo, from this time forth, henceforth, henceforwards (in the future, opp. abhinc).
Cum futuro: si ante quidem mentitus est, nunc jam dehinc erit verax tibi,; cf.: at ut scias, nunc dehinc latine jam loquar,; .—
Cum praes.: profecto nemo est, quem jam dehinc metuam,; ; so, ut quiescant,: ne exspectetis,: cf.: juro me L. Tarquinium Superbum ferro, igni, quacunque dehinc vi possim, exsecuturum,.—
With imperat.: at nunc dehinc scito, illum, etc.,; cf. . —
Referring to a point of time in the past, thenceforwards, since then: cum ex instituto Tiberii omnes dehinc Caesares beneficia ... aliter rata non haberent,: duplex dehinc fama est,. —
Without respect to the term. a quo, pointing to a future time.
Hereupon, afterwards, next, then (not anteAug.): Eurum ad se Zephyrumque vocat, dehinc talia fatur,; ; ; 6, 678; : dehinc audito legionum tumultu raptim profectus, etc.,; ; ; : post-positum,; ; : quae postquam vates sic ore effatus amico est, Dona dehinc ... imperat ad naves ferri,: de qua dehinc dicam,; .—
In enumerations ( = deinde), then (rare, and, excepting once in Sall., not anteAug.): arduum videtur res gestas scribere: primum quod ... dehinc quia, etc.,; so after primum,; after primo,: incipiet putrescere, dehinc laxata ire in humorem ... tunc exsilient flumina, inde, etc.,.—Cf. Hand, Turs. II. pp. 229-232.

la:verb:dehonesto.html:
dĕ-hŏnesto, āre,
v. a., to disgrace, disparage, dishonor (once in Liv., otherwise post-Aug.; cf. dehonestamentum): famam maculari dehonestarique,; ; ; cf.: proavum infami opera,; fin.; 4, 74 al.; ; ; Just 7, 3, 4; cf.: Romanum imperium, Treb. Gall. 16: amicum,.
